justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture addresses R-01 and circulation requirements via Catalog Component, Circulation Component, and Patron Account Component within Core Services Container. The Web App (SPA) delivers self-service portals for patrons and staff, ensuring complete functional coverage of all requirements.
justifications.performance_efficiency: To meet R-05 (<800ms search), Search Container uses Elasticsearch, a Redis Caching Layer, and CDC Ingestion Listener for low-latency indexing. API Client performs request deduplication, while Connection Pooler and Read-Replica Routing Layer optimize database throughput. SLA tracking is enforced by Blackbox Exporter.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture provides explicit integration mechanisms with external systems via standard protocols: OAuth 2.0/OIDC for Identity Provider (IdP), HTTPS/REST for Payment Gateway, and signed webhooks for Notification Service. W3C Trace Context ensures cross-service tracing compatibility.
justifications.usability: Patron & Library Administrator / Staff access the system through Web App (SPA), which explicitly incorporates WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Telemetry Wrapper tracks Core Web Vitals and Real User Monitoring to verify and maintain end-user interface usability.
justifications.reliability: High availability and fault tolerance are ensured via Patroni Primary-Replica Cluster, Elasticsearch Kubernetes StatefulSet, and RabbitMQ with Dead Letter Queues. API Gateway implements circuit breaking and rate limiting with Resilience4j, while Prometheus and Blackbox Exporter monitor system health.
justifications.security: EU-only data residency is enforced by Data Access Layer across EU private subnets with AES-256 encryption. Security mechanisms include Auth Filter with OAuth2/OIDC JWTs, mTLS, HashiCorp Vault dynamic credentials, PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, and Fluentbit PII scrubbing.
justifications.maintainability: The system is decomposed into loosely coupled containers and components, separating Catalog Component, Circulation Component, and Search Router. Asynchronous messaging via RabbitMQ and CDC reduces direct coupling, while Distributed Tracing Filter supports debuggability and maintainability.
justifications.portability: All elements (Web App (SPA), Core Services Container, Search Container, PostgreSQL) use containerized technologies (Nginx, Spring Boot, Kubernetes StatefulSet) capable of running across any EU cloud or on-premise infrastructure without vendor lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Elasticsearch 3-node cluster, Redis search cache, client query caching, and gateway rate limiting ensure sub-800ms P99 latency.
sensitivity_points: Redis cache hit ratio under high concurrency
Elasticsearch index sharding and query optimization
tradeoffs: Aggressive Redis query caching may briefly serve stale search results

PERF-02.justification: CQRS style decoupling via asynchronous CDC and message broker lets updates index in near real-time without impacting search.
sensitivity_points: Debezium CDC lag under heavy catalogue write loads
Search indexing throughput versus search query capacity
tradeoffs: Asynchronous replication favors query performance over immediate consistency

AVAIL-01.justification: A 3-node Elasticsearch StatefulSet tolerates single-node failure, and circulation is completely decoupled in PostgreSQL via Patroni.
sensitivity_points: Patroni automated consensus and failover time
tradeoffs: Multi-node index replication increases storage overhead and write replication costs

AVAIL-02.justification: Stateless SPA and gateway architecture allow seamless traffic rerouting, though SPA web server clustering is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Gateway health-check intervals for dead frontend instances
Stateless token validation across frontend reloads
tradeoffs: Stateless architecture requires client-side state recovery after instance failover

MOD-01.justification: Catalog Component encapsulates both physical and digital items, lacking a dedicated provider adapter layer for isolated e-book integration.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between external provider ingestion APIs and core catalog domain models
tradeoffs: Keeping digital cataloging within Catalog Component reduces microservice count but hampers extensibility

MOD-02.justification: No configuration-driven rule engine or policy store is defined; loan rules are hardcoded within the Circulation Component.
sensitivity_points: Absence of runtime dynamic configuration or externalized business rule engine
tradeoffs: Hardcoded domain service logic is simple to test but requires redeployment

SEC-01.justification: EU data residency is enforced via EU-only private subnets, EU-hosted notification and payment gateways, and explicit data-layer constraints.
sensitivity_points: Regional pinning of external SaaS provider endpoints
tradeoffs: Restricting providers to EU regions reduces options for external service integrations

SEC-02.justification: Cross-patron access is prevented through JWT verification, Spring Security @PreAuthorize, PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, and pgaudit logging.
sensitivity_points: JWT tenant and user claim extraction accuracy
tradeoffs: RLS evaluation and comprehensive audit logging add minor latency to database queries
